decisive_items: After 10 days of fever with an absolute neutrophil count of 20/μL
High-resolution chest CT showed nonspecific nodules under 1 cm
MRI of the right shoulder demonstrated a focal cystic necrotic lesion between the teres minor and teres major muscles.
response.rationale: Persistent fever with profound neutropenia, pulmonary nodules, and a new focal necrotic muscle lesion favor an invasive fungal infection; herpes zoster is suggested by pain but lacks vesicles and an MRI correlate, while febrile neutropenia and ALL are background/context.

rejected.why: Febrile neutropenia is the initial complication, not the specific diagnosis of the persistent fever and shoulder lesion.
No vesicles were present and MRI showed a cystic necrotic lesion, not dermatomal herpes zoster.
ALL is the established underlying leukemia, not the new focal infectious process.
